newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index falls on financial sector losses.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index falls on financial sector losses.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mixed in heavier trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, with financial sector share losses pushing the bourse lower.
The SAX index dipped 1.43 points to 202.1.
"The index is falling to its lowest levels in the past few months, mainly as a result of the decline in bank and insurance issues," Libor Briska of Creditanstalt said.
Insurance company Slovenska Poistovna (SP), one of 12 shares included in the index, was one of the hardest hit, closing down 220 crowns at 1,680, though only one share was traded.
"Though the minor volume traded in SP today does not seem transparent, we can still see a longer-term downward trend in all financial institutions, including banks VUB and IRB," Briska said.
The country's largest commercial bank VUB closed up 30 crowns at 1,650, but posted a 0.24 percent loss in its average price, on 103 traded shares.
Oil and gas storage firm Nafta closed down 30 at 1,970 crowns on 21,374 shares, after Tuesday's shareholders' meeting replaced a majority of firm's supervisory board.
"Big stakes changing hands in Nafta in these days are only settlements of earlier-agreed deals," Briska said.
He added the market was currently waiting for the new owner of Nafta to announce its plans for the company.
Overall volume increased to 707,793 shares, from 257,358 shares traded on Monday, while turnover, boosted by direct o-t-c trades, climbed to 579.68 million crowns, from 166.85 million.
